protocol.name: cutefish_shell_v1

description.summary: the desktop surface of the trusted session client

protocol.description:
This protocol lets the trusted client the session starts on its own connection (the file manager's daemon) say that a surface is the desktop of an output: below every window, kept to the output, told the work area its icons go in.
It is an *extension* of an ordinary wl_surface, not a replacement for xdg-shell. The client keeps creating xdg_toplevel objects through xdg_wm_base exactly like any other Wayland client; this protocol only adds the role, the output, the focus policy and the work area that plain xdg-shell cannot express.
The compositor only advertises this global on the one trusted connection it was handed by the session. Ordinary applications never see it.
Warning! Not a standard protocol. Backward-incompatible changes are made by bumping the interface version.

entry.name: role
entry.summary: the wl_surface already has a cutefish_shell_surface_v1

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroying the factory does not destroy the shell surfaces it created.

request.name: get_shell_surface

description.summary: extend a wl_surface with shell metadata

request.description:
Creates a cutefish_shell_surface_v1 for the given wl_surface.
The wl_surface must belong to the same client and the same connection. Giving a surface two shell surfaces raises the role error.
The metadata carried by the new object should be set before the first buffer is committed on the surface, so the compositor never has to place the surface as an ordinary window first.

interface.name: cutefish_shell_surface_v1

description.summary: shell metadata attached to a wl_surface

interface.description: Describes what the compositor should make of a shell surface. All state here takes effect immediately rather than on the next wl_surface.commit: the shell sets it once when the surface is created and the compositor applies it to the window the surface's xdg role produces.

enum.name: role
enum.description: The desktop of its output: stacked below every window, over the compositor's wallpaper, and covering the output.

entry.name: normal
entry.summary: the window can take keyboard focus

entry.name: no_focus
entry.summary: the window receives pointer input but never keyboard focus

request.name: destroy
request.description: The surface goes back to being an ordinary window.

request.name: set_role
request.description: Must be sent before the surface is first mapped. Changing the role of a mapped surface is allowed but the compositor may only apply it the next time the surface is mapped.

request.name: activate

description.summary: give this surface the keyboard focus

request.description:
The trusted way for the desktop to take the keyboard, as it does once when first shown. No serial is required: the client is trusted, and this activation does not come from an input event it can point at.
Ignored while the surface has no window, or while its focus policy is no_focus.

request.name: set_output

description.summary: associate this surface with a logical output

request.description: Selects the logical output by its stable wl_output name. A desktop is placed at its output's origin, by default the primary output's, and follows it when the layout changes; the client sizes it to the output.

event.name: work_area

description.summary: where a desktop lays out its content

event.description: Sent to a desktop surface: its output's bounds less what the compositor's own panels and every exclusive zone reserve, where windows are laid out. In surface-local logical pixels, the surface being placed at its output's origin. Sent once the surface is a desktop, before its first configure, and again whenever the work area or the surface's output changes.
